svg.title: A short history of the actor model
svg.desc: A timeline. 1973: Hewitt, Bishop and Steiger publish the actor formalism at IJCAI. 1985: Agha's report defines what an actor does with a message: send messages, create actors, and pick its behavior for the next message. 1986: Erlang starts at the Ericsson Computer Science Laboratory, for programming telephony applications. 1996: the OTP project starts, with supervisors and workers. 1998: Open Source Erlang is released in December. 2003: Joe Armstrong's thesis describes "let it crash" and supervision trees. 2009: Akka, actors on the JVM, starts. 2014: Microsoft Research describes Orleans and virtual actors. 2026: lockstep v0.1.0 brings typed actors to Go with deterministic simulation testing.
